pages.class_justification: The constructed OWF is $G$ itself, so the construction uses the hypothesis PRG only as an oracle; the security reduction runs any inverter once as an oracle and accepts iff the returned $\hat{x}$ satisfies $G(\hat{x}) = y$. This is the RTV04 fully-black-box shape.
pages.statement: Any [[pseudorandom-generator|PRG]] $G : \bits^n \to \bits^m$ with $m > n$ is itself a [[hash-function#preimage-resistance-one-wayness|one-way function]]: an efficient inverter for $G$ yields a distinguisher, since a uniform $y \in \bits^m$ has a $G$-preimage with probability at most $2^{n-m}$ — folklore. Only one-wayness follows; a PRG does not generically yield collision resistance.
pages.sketch: The OWF is $G$ itself. Given an inverter $\calA$ succeeding with probability $\varepsilon$, the distinguisher $D(y)$ runs $\hat{x} \gets \calA(y)$ and outputs $1$ iff $G(\hat{x}) = y$: on $y = G(s)$ it outputs $1$ with probability $\varepsilon$, on uniform $y$ with probability at most $2^{n-m}$.
flags: Conclusion 'hash-function' is the wiki's combined hash/OWF page (alias OWF); the edge is PRG => OWF, and the statement pins the preimage-resistance variant via the page's declared anchor #preimage-resistance-one-wayness. PRG => collision-resistant hashing does NOT hold black-box (Simon, EUROCRYPT 1998 oracle separation) — not proposed as a source because it could not be verified online in this session (eprint/DBLP/arXiv egress-blocked, search budget exhausted).

The migrated quote's trailing 'so OWF <=> PRG' is a derived equivalence: the converse direction is [[hash-function-to-prg-hill99]] (HILL99). Both directions exist as separate pages, so this page correctly stays kind: implication.
The length-expansion hypothesis ($m > n$) is load-bearing and is definitional for the wiki's PRG page; the statement carries it explicitly.

sources.ref_file_title: GGM86 - How to construct random functions
sources.authors: Oded Goldreich, Shafi Goldwasser, Silvio Micali
sources.note: Verified against vendor/cryptobib entry GolGolMic86 (JACM 33(4):792-807, 1986, doi 10.1145/6490.6503) and the existing wiki reference page.

pages.class_justification: The construction invokes the length-doubling PRG only as an oracle (one call per input bit); the security proof is a hybrid argument over the tree levels whose reduction runs any PRF distinguisher as an oracle to build a PRG distinguisher. The wiki's black-box-separations page uses this construction as its worked example of the fully-black-box notion.
pages.statement: A length-doubling [[pseudorandom-generator|PRG]] $G : \bits^n \to \bits^{2n}$ yields a [[pseudorandom-function|PRF]] with keyspace and range $\bits^n$ and domain $\bits^\ell$: writing $G(s) = G_0(s) \| G_1(s)$, define $\Eval(k, x_1 \cdots x_\ell) := G_{x_\ell}(G_{x_{\ell-1}}(\cdots G_{x_1}(k) \cdots))$ — [[GGM86 - How to construct random functions|GGM86]].
pages.sketch: The construction walks a binary tree of depth $\ell$: start from $k$ and, on bit $x_i$, keep the left or right half of $G$'s output. A hybrid over the $\ell$ tree levels reduces any $q$-query PRF distinguisher to a PRG distinguisher, with a factor $q\ell$ security loss.
flags: The factor-$q\ell$ loss in the sketch is the standard textbook hybrid analysis (e.g. Boneh-Shoup Thm 4.11), not a concrete bound stated in GGM86 itself (which is asymptotic); security_loss left empty for that reason.

pages.class_justification: Composition of two fully-black-box links: the GGM construction calls the PRG only as an oracle, and PRF-based randomized encryption calls the PRF only as an oracle; each security reduction runs the adversary as an oracle, and fully-black-box reductions compose. The composed construction/reduction pair retains the RTV04 fully-black-box shape.
pages.statement: A [[pseudorandom-generator|PRG]] implies CPA-secure [[symmetric-key-encryption|SKE]]: a length-doubling PRG yields a [[pseudorandom-function|PRF]] ([[prg-to-prf-ggm86|PRG ⇒ PRF (GGM)]]), and encrypting as $\Enc(k, m) = (r, \Eval(k, r) \oplus m)$ with fresh random $r$ is CPA-secure ([[prf-to-ske|PRF ⇒ CPA-secure SKE]]) — folklore. The fixed-pad stream cipher $\Enc(k, m) = G(k) \oplus m$ is deterministic and therefore not CPA-secure; it achieves only one-time security.
flags: CONFIRMED ERROR in the migrated statement (not in the edge): $\Enc(k,m) = G(k) \oplus m$ reuses one pad for every message, so two left-right oracle queries break CPA security; the scheme is only one-time secure. The edge PRG => CPA-SKE itself is true via the PRF route. The parent page content/Primitives/pseudorandom-generator.md still carries the wrong bullet and is already flagged in .fact-check/queue.json — fix it in the same commit that applies this page.

Composite-chain page: both links exist as prg-to-prf-ggm86 and prf-to-ske, so per schema/README this edge is derivable; consider deleting it or rescoping to 'PRG => one-time-secure SKE' (direct stream cipher). Rescoping is blocked today because the SKE page defines no one-time/EAV security notion to target.

pages.class_justification: The iPRF is the PRP itself with $\Invert$ wrapped to return the singleton preimage set; both algorithms call the PRP only as oracles. The security reduction runs any distinguisher unchanged as a PRP distinguisher, absorbing the ideal-world gap into the information-theoretic switching-lemma term.
pages.statement: A [[pseudorandom-permutation|PRP]] over a domain $\calD$ of superpolynomial size is an [[pseudorandom-function#invertible-prfs|invertible PRF]] with respect to the traditional (forward-oracle) PRF security game: set the iPRF's inversion algorithm to return the singleton $\{\Invert(k, y)\}$, and bound any $q$-query distinguisher's advantage by the PRP advantage plus the [[switching-lemma|Switching Lemma]] term $O(q^2/|\calD|)$ — folklore. Strong iPRF security, in which the adversary also queries an inversion oracle, does not follow.
pages.sketch: A permutation is an iPRF with singleton preimage sets and perfect correctness. For forward queries only, a random permutation is statistically within $O(q^2/|\calD|)$ of a random function, so PRP security transfers to the traditional PRF game with birthday loss.
pages.security_loss: $O(q^2/|\calD|)$ for $q$ queries, per the switching lemma
notes_to_keep: The iPRF strong security game gives $\calA$ an inversion oracle, so the forward-only switching lemma does not justify the strong reading; the statement above is scoped to the traditional forward-oracle game. This is flagged against both parent pages in the fact-check queue.
flags: The strong-iPRF reading is not merely unproven but FALSE for every PRP under the wiki's $\Game^{\mathrm{iprf}}$ as defined on pseudorandom-function.md: the ideal world is a random function with a preimage-SET oracle, and a fresh inversion query returns a singleton for any permutation but the empty set with probability about $1/e$ for a random function on $\calD \to \calD$ — a one-query distinguisher with constant advantage. The existing fact-check suggestion that 'sPRP plus a two-sided switching lemma' would suffice is therefore itself incorrect for this game (a two-sided switching lemma compares against a random permutation with inverse oracle, not a random function with preimage-set oracle). The honest fix is exactly the scoping in the statement above.

HPPY25 (Plinko), which introduced the iPRF notion cited by the sibling page prf-to-invertible-prf-hppy25, does not state this PRP observation in its abstract; the claim is left folklore with the switching lemma as the technique (kept in via:).

sources.ref_file_title: Din20 - On the Streaming Indistinguishability of a Random Permutation and a Random Function
sources.note: Already cited on the wiki's switching-lemma page for the memory-bounded improvement.

pages.class_justification: The construction is the identity: the PRP's $\Eval$ is used unchanged as the PRF (the hypothesis is invoked only as an oracle). The security reduction runs any PRF distinguisher once, unchanged, as a PRP distinguisher; the remaining ideal-world gap (random permutation vs. random function) is the information-theoretic switching-lemma term, needing no access to the adversary's code.
pages.statement: A [[pseudorandom-permutation|PRP]] over a domain $\calD$ of superpolynomial size is a [[pseudorandom-function|PRF]]: the permutation is used unchanged, and any $q$-query distinguisher's advantage grows by at most the [[switching-lemma|Switching Lemma]] term $O(q^2/|\calD|)$, which is negligible for superpolynomial $|\calD|$ — [[BKR00 - The Security of the Cipher Block Chaining Message Authentication Code|BKR00]].
pages.sketch: In the ideal worlds, a random permutation and a random function on $\calD$ are statistically indistinguishable up to the birthday bound $O(q^2/|\calD|)$ — an output collision is the only distinguishing event — so any PRF distinguisher is a PRP distinguisher with an additive $O(q^2/|\calD|)$ advantage loss.
pages.improvements_text:
- Game-playing proof of the switching lemma, correcting the conditioning flaw in the folklore proof — [[BR06 - The Security of Triple Encryption and a Framework for Code-Based Game-Playing Proofs|BR06]]
- For streaming distinguishers with $m$ bits of memory the bound improves to $O(mq/|\calD|)$ — [[Din20 - On the Streaming Indistinguishability of a Random Permutation and a Random Function|Din20]]
flags: The birthday switching argument is older folklore (arguably implicit in IR89's key-exchange lower bound); BKR00 is proposed as the first recorded concrete-security statement, following BR06's attribution. pages.statement: $\classPSPACE \subseteq \classEXP$: a deterministic machine using space $p(n) = \poly(n)$ has at most $2^{O(p(n))}$ configurations, so it either halts within $2^{O(p(n))}$ steps or cycles forever; simulating it for that many steps decides its language in exponential time — folklore.

pages.statement: $\classQCMA \subseteq \classQMA$: a QCMA verifier becomes a QMA verifier by measuring the witness register in the computational basis and running the QCMA verification on the outcome. Completeness is preserved by sending the classical witness as a basis state; soundness is preserved because measurement turns any quantum witness into a distribution over classical strings and the acceptance probability is the average over that distribution — folklore.
